scan.pinterest_status: Pinterest's official Business and Newsroom results, the 2026 Hobbies Trend Report, Creator workflow guidance, the 2026 Palette and relevant public Pinterest inspiration were checked on 25 October 2026. No newer official trend publication appeared after the 23 October BFCM guidance. Hobbies signals around zines, edited collections, analog craft, tactile making and cyberdeck/tech makeovers remain relevant but do not reveal an uncovered production capability.
scan.chatgpt_status: Production v2.26.0 with 721 commands was read before evaluation. /zine-editorial-system covers publication structure and typography; /analog-keepsake covers tactile archival storytelling; /taste-discovery-system and /trend-to-brand cover identity-led curation and translation; /content-lifecycle-system covers planning, reuse and feedback. The 23 October BFCM guidance remains covered by /intent-to-action, /performance-creative-mix and /catalog-creative-system. No materially new command was warranted. The userscript and metadata remained byte-identical, and all 22 regression checks passed.
trends: Hands-on hobbies continue to favour tactile craft, edited collections, analog practice and satisfying real-world outputs
Zine revival spans digital magazine layouts, book logs, printables, journals, photo albums and physical tunnel books
Cyberdeck and tech-makeover interest combines retro-futurist hardware, terminal aesthetics and personalised packaging-scale details
Creator workflows continue to connect trend research, board-based planning, portfolio/collage storytelling, reuse and analytics-led refresh
Pinterest Predicts continues to favour identity curation, personal remixing, nostalgia and grounded optimism
The 2026 Palette remains a cross-category colour framework rather than a need for one-command-per-colour aliases
skipped: No Handmade Hacker or Zine Revival command because /zine-editorial-system, /analog-keepsake and /content-lifecycle-system already cover modular publication, tactile sequencing, collage and reuse

No cyberdeck or terminal-aesthetic command because the signal is a topical styling route that /trend-to-brand, /retro-pop-branding, /moodboard and existing tech/cinematic controls can translate without a dedicated alias
No Kitchen Witch, Cosmic Reset or other hobby-name aliases because they are seasonal motifs rather than reusable production capabilities
No new BFCM command because /intent-to-action, /performance-creative-mix, /catalog-creative-system and /content-lifecycle-system already cover staged intent, product truth and conversion paths
No individual 2026 Palette or Pinterest Predicts aliases because existing palette, taste, visual-style and trend-translation commands already support controlled cross-category adaptation
Public Pinterest inspiration repeated zine layouts, cyberdeck objects and established 2026 graphic-design themes without a distinct workflow gap
